subject: Architecture
title: The Millau Viaduct: Highway in the Clouds
description: One-minute skill: The Millau Viaduct: Highway in the Clouds.

hook.text: The Millau Viaduct in France is taller than the Eiffel Tower — cars drive through clouds.

buildup.text: At 1,125 feet, its tallest pier makes it the highest bridge in the world, spanning the Tarn Valley.

discovery.text: Norman Foster designed it to be as thin as possible — the deck is only 14 feet deep despite spanning 1,122 feet.

twist.text: The deck was built on both sides of the valley and pushed out over the void — sliding into position.

climax.text: Drivers report feeling like they're flying. The bridge eliminates a bottleneck that caused 4-hour delays.

punchline.text: A road through the sky. Built to save you from traffic.

quiz.question: How was the Millau Viaduct's deck constructed?
options: Lifted into place by the world's largest crane
Built from both sides and pushed out to meet in the middle
Assembled on the ground and raised hydraulically

details.summary: The Millau Viaduct in southern France stands 343 meters tall at its highest point — taller than the Eiffel Tower. Designed by Norman Foster and engineer Michel Virlogeux.
details.whyItMatters: The Millau Viaduct proves that even massive infrastructure can be elegant. By treating a highway bridge as an architectural design problem, Foster and Virlogeux created a structure that enhances rather than scars the landscape it crosses.
takeaways: Stands 343 meters tall — taller than the Eiffel Tower
Seven cable-stayed pylons carry a motorway across a valley
Designed jointly by architect Norman Foster and engineer Virlogeux

faq.question: How was the Millau Viaduct built across such a wide valley?
faq.answer: The deck was assembled behind the south abutment and launched forward incrementally, sliding on temporary pylons until reaching each permanent pier. GPS-guided hydraulic rams moved the 36,000-ton deck forward in 600mm increments with centimeter accuracy.

faq.question: Why was this route chosen over a valley-floor road?
faq.answer: Traffic bottlenecks in the town of Millau below caused massive summer delays on the route from Paris to Spain. A high viaduct bypassed the valley entirely, reducing the journey time through the area from hours to minutes while preserving the town below.
